text:
Alex: Heads-up — after the dual-stack roll in prod-us-west2 we're seeing intermittent packet loss east-west between GPU nodes. RTT spikes 0.5–30ms, and some flows get routed to strange v6 pod IPs on other nodes. Affected hosts are RDMA-enabled. Anyone seen this?

Maria: Can you share `ip -6 route` from one of the problematic nodes and a `tracepath6` to a pod IP? Also, which CNI and kernel?

Alex: CNI=cilium v1.14 (eBPF mode), kernel=5.15. Here's a trimmed `ip -6 route` from node-12: 

```
::ffff:0.0.0.0 via fe80::1 dev eth0 proto kernel metric 100
fd00:10:0:1::/64 via fe80::5a1 dev cilium_host proto static
fd00:10:0:2::/64 dev cilium_vxlan scope link
::/0 via fe80::2 dev eth0 proto static
```

Alex: And `tracepath6 fd00:10:0:2::123` sometimes shows a hop that resolves to a v6 address from node-07 even though pod is scheduled on node-12.

Jin: Interesting — dual-stack plus eBPF CNIs sometimes leave stale host routes when node IPs change. Do you see duplicate `fe80` next-hops in `ip -6 neigh`? Also check `cilium operator` logs for "invalid next-hop" warnings.

Alex: `ip -6 neigh` shows a few dangling entries pointing to node-07 MACs for addresses that should be on node-12.

Sam: Two possibilities we've hit before: (1) MTU / fragmentation differences between overlay and host path causing IPv6 path MTU blackhole, (2) Cilium's host-routing incorrectly preferring a learned route from BGP/underlay that maps to the wrong node when dual-stack translations happen. RDMA complicates things because we prefer host-device networking and bypass overlay.

Dina: Related note — a couple of the RDMA nodes still had MTU 1450 on eth0 (cloud LB path) while the rest of cluster uses 9000 (jumbo). IPv6 packets with extension headers + DF can get dropped or result in fragmentation. Run `ip -6 route get <pod-ip>` and `tracepath6 -n` to see MTU along path.

Alex: Ran `tracepath6` with `-n`, got `pmtu 1450` at an intermediate hop.

Jin: If pmtu is lower, and the CNI encap overhead isn't accounted for, fragmentation drops could manifest as packet loss, and some control flows (ARP/ND) might time out and lead to transient misroutes. Also confirm whether cilium is doing encapsulation for v6 traffic (vxlan/geneve) — overlay encap can be asymmetric between IPv4/IPv6.

Maria: Can you post `cilium status --all` and `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=cilium -o wide` for the nodes? Also any custom iptables/nft rules for IPv6 installed by customers or egress appliances?

Alex: Posting short `cilium status` excerpt: 

```
KVStore:             Ok   Disabled
Cilium:              Ok   Running
Operator:             Ok   Running
HostRouting:         Warning  some host routes unresolved
```

Alex: We do have an egress firewall (managed) that has dual-stack rules; I checked and it should be just routing, not NAT.

Sam: Another angle — RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet) requires certain priorities; when we switched to dual-stack we also flipped kernel sysctls that touched `rp_filter`/`accept_redirects` maybe. Verify `sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects` and `rp_filter` settings. Accept redirects on ipv6 can rewrite routes if a middlebox sends redirects.

Dina: Quick checks I ran on a repro node: `sysctl net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects = 1` on node-07 (bad), while others have it 0. Changing it to 0 eliminated the incorrect neighbor-learning messages.

Alex: That matches — node-07 had a leftover setting from an older golden image. Noted. We still see intermittent latency spikes though.

Jin: For the RDMA nodes, we should avoid overlay encap for v6 and use host-local L2 bridging or direct routes. Cilium has an option to enable `enable-ipv6` + `autoDirectNodeRoutes` — but watch for kernel bug interplay. Suggest: for RDMA node pool, switch to host-routes (no encap) for IPv6 and ensure MTU matches.

Maria: Action items: (1) Set `net.ipv6.conf.*.accept_redirects=0` on all prod nodes (hotfix), (2) align MTU to 9000 or standardize to 1450 across affected network path and re-run calico/cilium mtu config, (3) for RDMA node pool, enable host-local routing for v6 and roll back overlay encap, (4) open ticket with Cilium with `cilium bugtool` dump.

OpsBot: Incident alert #INC-2026-378 opened for "prod-us-west2 IPv6 dual-stack misroutes". Priority=P2. Links: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-378

Alex: I'll start the hotfix for accept_redirects and schedule a canary for host-routes on two RDMA nodes. Will attach `cilium bugtool` output once collected. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
